caption: The drawing depicts an interior architectural scene with various decorative elements. Central to the composition is a large, arched alcove or niche that is framed in red, with an ornate blue and red trim at the top, and a small cross above it. Flanking the alcove are two columns that support pointed arches, outlined in red and decorated with alternating red and white segments and blue accents. Above the alcove, the arches have repeating triangular designs with blue highlights pointing downward. On the left side, there is a circular motif with a radiating edge, a blue triangular center, and it is supported by a red, chalice-like base with an inverted 'V' shape. Below this motif runs a low wall or balustrade marked by small repeating red shapes, each topped with a small cross, and blue accents underneath. The lower section of the drawing features a checkerboard pattern in red and white on the wall at the left and beneath the alcove, with additional red diamond shapes scattered across the surface. The floor is sketched with a faint blue outline and tan washes. The color palette primarily includes shades of red, blue, brown, and beige, and the background is rendered in a light, uneven wash suggesting plastered or aged stonework.
title: Wall Painting and Baptismal Niche
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
